readings: Input register stage + partial-sum register stage + final product register = mul_en_out asserted 3 cycles after mul_en_in (3-stage pipeline)

Only the input register and the final mul_out_reg are clocked stages, giving a 2-cycle latency; or splitting partial sums into two register stages gives 4 cycles. mul_en_out timing differs by 1-2 cycles for the same input.

mul_en_out_reg (and the data pipeline) shift/advance every clock unconditionally, so gaps between valid input samples propagate and mul_en_out is high only for the cycles corresponding to valid mul_en_in pulses

All registers update only when their stage's enable is active (as stated for the input registers), so a single mul_en_in pulse leaves mul_en_out high for several consecutive cycles and back-to-back products cannot be pipelined
rst_n asynchronously clears every state element (mul_a_reg, mul_b_reg, partial-sum regs, mul_out_reg, mul_en_out_reg) to 0 on the same edge
rst_n is synchronous and/or only the explicitly described registers are cleared, so sum[]/mul_out_reg power up undefined and mul_out may be X until the first valid product
mul_out is a purely combinational mux: mul_out = mul_en_out ? mul_out_reg : 16'h0, so it is 0 in the same cycle mul_en_out is low
mul_out is itself registered, so it holds the last product for one extra cycle after mul_en_out falls (or is cleared one cycle later), changing the cycle-by-cycle output waveform
